title: Bharat Forge Aerospace

body.raw:
## Project Overview

Automation and Sensor Integration academic project conducted at **Bharat Forge Aerospace** in Pune, India from April 2026 to July 2026.

### Contributions

*   **Electromechanical Design:** Translated 3D CAD layouts into a fully operational electromechanical system architecture.
*   **Sensor Selection:** Selected proximity, optical, and thickness sensors/actuators against strict aerospace tolerance requirements via datasheet evaluation.

title: EMBER GPU
description: A GPU designed from scratch: custom rasterization, floating-point, tensor, and compute hardware, verified in simulation and taken through routed SkyWater 130 nm layouts.

body.raw:
## Project Overview

I built a GPU from scratch. Not a simulation of a GPU — an actual chip design: my own rasterizer, my own floating-point unit, my own instruction set, and my own tensor core. The RTL runs graphics and inference demos in simulation, and several blocks now have routed, DRC-checked GDS layouts.

The entire project was built on one Windows/WSL machine using an open-source toolchain.

![EMBER GPU architecture diagram](/projects/ember-gpu/architecture.png)

## Hardware Architecture

* **Command processor:** A command processor with DMA and fences, driving everything through one AXI4-Lite bus.
* **Rasterizer:** A multi-cycle rasterizer with a Z-buffer, CLUT textures, alpha blending, and dithering — the whole PS1-era output stage implemented in logic.
* **Vector FPU:** A four-lane IEEE-754 fp32 vector FPU written from the gates up, with round-to-nearest-even, subnormal, and NaN handling. Getting the rounding modes right took two weeks and taught me more about floating point than any course.
* **Tensor core:** A 16×16 int8 systolic tensor array that runs a real CNN. A trained LeNet reads an actual MNIST digit and names it, reaching 98% accuracy, with RTL byte-for-byte identical to the software model.
* **Compute core:** A four-thread compute core with its own 32-bit ISA and assembler runs the game's physics. The camera walking through the temple is integrated every frame by instructions the GPU executes itself.

## Verification

The verification suite passes 31/31 tests against independent Python golden models, bit-exact — every pixel and every byte of every layer.

## RTL to GDS-II

The RTL-to-layout flow uses sv2v, Yosys, OpenROAD, Magic, and KLayout on the open SkyWater 130 nm process. The blocks go through floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, detailed routing, design-rule checking, and GDS-II export, producing real polygons a foundry tool can open.

## Project Documentation

Source code and project updates are available on [GitHub](https://github.com/toshalkumbhar8979-design). Project images and routed-layout views will be added to the gallery as they are ready.

title: Imitation Learning-Based Autonomous Robotic Arm

body.raw:
## Project Overview

Engineered a custom 6-DOF robotic manipulator from June 2026, driven by an Arduino Uno and PCA9685 PWM driver over I2C.

### Contributions

* Implemented a 115200-baud binary serial protocol with a 500 ms watchdog for fail-safe actuation.
* Built a FastAPI and WebSockets control system streaming at 30 Hz, with a 3D URDF digital twin and live switching between Cartesian inverse kinematics and direct joint control.

* Extended the system with ROS 2, MoveIt, and Gazebo for live remote control of the physical arm through its simulated digital twin.

title: RISC-V RV32IM SoC with RTL to GDS-II Sign-off
description: A complete open RISC-V system-on-chip designed, verified, and taken through a DRC-clean GDS-II layout on SkyWater 130 nm.

body.raw:
## Project Overview

Designed a RISC-V RV32IM system-on-chip from scratch, including a 2-stage pipelined core with the M-extension, CSRs, interrupts, and a complete peripheral set. The SoC boots software from QSPI flash and provides a DOOM-compatible platform, then passes through the complete OpenLane 2 physical-design flow on SkyWater 130 nm.

## Key Highlights

*   **RV32IM Core:** Built a Verilog-2001 2-stage pipeline with multiply/divide, CSR and trap/mret support, and timer interrupts. Self-checking testbenches pass both the core and M-extension unit tests.
*   **SoC Integration:** Connected BootROM, 32 KB SRAM, QSPI flash XIP, SPI-TFT (ILI9341), UART, and mtime/mtimecmp. The end-to-end SoC test passes boot, flash copy, display pattern, timer IRQ, and PASS mailbox checks.
*   **Software Stack:** Built the GNU RISC-V cross-compiler flow, linker script, crt0, platform HAL, and `doomgeneric` bindings for a C demo that boots and runs on the SoC.
*   **RTL to GDS-II:** Ran synthesis, placement, CTS, routing, DRC, LVS, and GDS-II export with OpenLane 2 and the volare SkyWater 130 nm PDK. The probe design closed with 0 DRC violations, 0 LVS mismatches, timing met at 20 ns, 18,267 cells, 0.28 mm² area, 8.3 mW power, and +8.8 ns setup slack.
*   **Full-SoC Synthesis:** Reached 68,690 cells and 0.916 mm², with 43% sequential logic, through CTS with 1,952 clock subnets and WNS of 0.

## Technology Stack

Verilog, RISC-V, Icarus Verilog, GNU RISC-V toolchain, Yosys, OpenROAD, OpenLane 2, SkyWater 130 nm, Magic, KLayout, Netgen, QSPI, UART, SPI-TFT, and WSL2.

## Project Documentation

[Read the project paper](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LuWkrK-gQlqWzloCvj7BRWznMQ1FX8mW/view?usp=sharing)

## Further Work

OpenRAM hard-macro integration for the SRAM, full-corner timing closure, and FPGA board bring-up.

body.raw:
## Project Overview

Built a modular C/C++ firmware and analysis framework for interfacing sensors, streaming telemetry, and validating control logic during hardware bring-up.

### Peripheral Drivers & Telemetry

*   **Sensor Interfaces:** Connected proximity, optical, and IMU-class sensors over I2C and UART with configurable sampling and non-blocking reads.
*   **Binary Logging:** Implemented a lightweight telemetry logger that streamed timestamped sensor data and status flags to a host over serial for live monitoring and offline post-processing.
*   **Offline Analysis:** Wrote Python tools to parse field-style logs, compute statistics, detect anomalies, and visualize trends during bring-up and validation.
*   **Software-in-the-Loop Testing:** Added harnesses that replayed recorded logs against control logic to verify edge-case handling and fault containment without physical hardware.

*   **Communication:** I2C, UART, serial telemetry
*   **Analysis:** Python, statistical analysis, anomaly detection, data visualization
